newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila bourse loses lustre, dives again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila bourse loses lustre, dives again.

text.p: Philippine shares ran out of steam as profit-taking pushed the market down by nearly three percent in what analysts said was a major technical correction after a sparkling two-day rally.

The main index lost 82 points to settle at 2,694.40 as waves of selling cut the legs from under the market, sweeping blue chips like Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, San Miguel Corp B and Manila Electic Co B.
Research head Dennis Rayala of Abacus Securities said he saw the drop as a major technical correction and could be part of a consolidation phase.
"I think a lot of people were just questioning themselves what was really the logic behind what we did the past two days," Rayala said.
"After rethinking their positions, and the lingering concerns on real estate, banking and even the macro economic conditions, they decided to question whether this is sustainable." he said.
Fears the real estate sector had overheated had sent share prices of property firms and banks believed to have large loan exposures to the sector crashing in the past few weeks.
Losers routed gainers 110 to 20 and all sub-indices fell sharply, led by the commercial-industrial index.
At one point, the key index briefly plunged 3.06 percent to 2,692.29 points.
Traders said the correction was expected as the market's barometer had surged by 170.88 points, or 6.55 percent, to 2,776.53 in just two days from Friday's 2,605,65.
PLDT shed 35 pesos to close at 745 pesos, Metrobank lost 10 pesos to 590, San Miguel B dropped three pesos to 68 pesos while Meralco B skidded nine pesos and wound up at 129.
"This is a bad sign. This decline will likely continue until tommorrow and we may even test the 2,600 support," said Henry Ong, dealer at Sapphire Securities.
"I'll be more woried if we go down below 2,600," one analyst said, adding he expected the market to trade trade sideways in a very volatile band within the next few days. Conversion $1 = 26.3 pesos
